comments.body:
## RCA evidence for this ticket's acceptance criteria (from incident `bafc-2f85-836f-4bdd` / `decrepit-blowy-javalina`)

Two answers were requested. The second one **invalidates this ticket's replay criterion as written** — please correct it before anyone implements.

### 1. Observed duplicate count and rate

Measured over the whole rebar store (5,329 non-archived tickets) and the live binding store (`.bridge_state/bindings.json` @ `origin/tickets`, 5,333 entries):

- **89 normalized titles** have more than one ticket.
- **425 excess tickets** (total copies minus one per title).
- **425 of 425 are bound to Jira**, each to a distinct key — Jira range **REB-665..REB-4415**.
- **389 of the 425** have rebar status != closed, i.e. they are the open Jira duplicates the operator sees.
- Worst offenders: 12x `a2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping...`, 9x each for seven `comment triage: <area>` titles, 8x several `size relief: ...` titles.

**Rate, for threshold-setting:**

| window | excess duplicate tickets created |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-31 (whole day) | 233 |
| 2026-09-01 (whole day) | 172 |
| peak hour 08-31 23:00Z | 88 |
| 08-31 06:00Z .. 09-01 04:00Z (the burst) | 345 |
| typical baseline (Jul-Aug, per day) | 0-2 |

A threshold of **>10 same-normalized-title excess creations per rolling hour** separates the burst (88/hr at peak, 6 consecutive hours above 20) from baseline (0-2/day) with ~an order of magnitude of headroom.

### 2. The duplicate signature — normalized title, as assumed. BUT the replay window is wrong.

**Signature: confirmed normalized title.** All 425 were found by exactly `re.sub(r'\s+',' ',title.strip().lower())` collision. `create_ticket`'s existing `duplicate_warning` (`_lib_writes.py:182`) uses the same signature and would have fired on every one. No rewrite of the criteria is needed on this axis.

Explicitly ruled out, so nobody has to re-derive it:
- **Zero** Jira keys are bound to more than one local ticket (5,333 bindings, 5,333 distinct keys). There is no "one rebar ticket, two Jira issues" duplicate class.
- The binding store grew monotonically through the whole incident and never lost an entry, so there is no binding-field-only duplicate class either.

**The replay criterion must change.** The ticket asks the detector to fire against store history for **2026-09-05 05:27-09:26 UTC** (the five long bridge passes). **Zero duplicate-title tickets were created in that window** — or anywhere in the 09-04/09-05 incident at all. A detector replayed there fires zero times and looks broken.

The correct replay window is **2026-08-31 06:00Z .. 2026-09-01 04:00Z**, where 345 excess creations occurred. Suggested criterion: replayed over that window the detector fires, and replayed over 2026-08-20..08-25 (baseline) it does not.

### 3. A second detector is needed — title collision would NOT have caught this incident

The 09-04/05 event that produced hundreds of new open Jira issues was **~1,700 tickets with distinct titles** (`Condense comments in <path>`, one per repo file), created 2026-09-04 19:00-01:00Z. Every title is unique, so `duplicate_warning` is silent by construction and correctly so.

The signal that would have caught it is **creation volume**, not collision:

- rebar side: local CREATE events/hour went 4-9 (steady) -> 62 -> 184 -> **968** -> 318.
- bridge side: `RECON: outbound_differ create=` went 0-4 (steady) -> 138 -> 520 -> **1180**.

Both are rebar-side signals — neither needs a Jira query, so neither inherits the ACLI 1,200 ceiling. The `create=` counter in particular is already printed every pass and already thrown away, exactly like `duplicate_warning`.

Recommend this ticket cover **two** detectors, or split the volume one out:
- **A. Collision detector** — aggregate `duplicate_warning`; threshold >10/rolling hour; replay 08-31 06:00Z..09-01 04:00Z.
- **B. Volume detector** — alarm on local CREATE events/hour and on per-pass `outbound_differ create=`; threshold ~10x trailing-7-day median; replay 09-04 19:00Z..09-05 02:00Z.

Detector A alone would have missed this incident entirely. That is the "quietly makes the whole alarm useless" outcome the ticket was worried about, and it is real — just on the volume axis rather than the signature axis.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Root cause is now PROVEN — and it changes what this detector is FOR

The 2026-09-05 `/rebar-debug` investigation on `anarchic-princely-raven` (`00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc`)
proved the producer of the 425 excess tickets: **rebar's own Tier-2 plan-replay eval harness,
writing into the LIVE store.** `materialize_reconstructed_ticket` builds its "throwaway scratch
tracker" with `git worktree add` on the ticket repo; a linked worktree has a `.git` FILE rather
than a directory, so `init.py:197-199` returns via `_init_via_symlink` BEFORE `force_new_store` is
consulted, symlinking the scratch store onto the real one. The harness ledger records exactly six
tier-2 runs, the last finishing `2026-09-01T03:36:48Z` — the same minute as the last duplicate,
matching six independently measured bursts.

That specific producer is being fixed. **This detector's value is therefore the NEXT unknown
producer**, not this one — build it to catch a symptom from any writer, not to catch the harness.

## CORRECTION to an argument in the previous comment

The previous comment lists as "explicitly ruled out, so nobody has to re-derive it":

> Zero Jira keys are bound to more than one local ticket (5,333 bindings, 5,333 distinct keys).
> There is no "one rebar ticket, two Jira issues" duplicate class.

The MEASUREMENT is fine; the INFERENCE is not, and it should not be relied on. The binding map is
keyed by rebar ticket id, so a re-create OVERWRITES the entry — an orphaned create (issue made,
binding write failed) is invisible in it. Distinctness proves the map is well-formed, not that
duplication did not occur. I made this exact error earlier and withdrew it.

Separately, the per-title Jira-vs-rebar COUNT-MATCH test is also non-discriminating: an inbound
echo via `_apply_inbound_create` creates one ticket on EACH side and preserves the match. Neither
test belongs in this ticket's evidence base. The reconciler was ultimately excluded, but on three
instruments that do not depend on either: zero bridge-authored CREATE commits in the burst window,
zero `jira-<key>`-namespaced ids among 495 burst creates, and one-pass convergence under
perturbation.

## TWO PRECISION REQUIREMENTS for detector A, measured tonight

Both are false-positive sources that will make a title-collision detector cry wolf and get muted:

**1. The normalizer folds distinct paths together.** The store's own `normalize_title`
(`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:55`) collapses `__init__.py` and `_init.py` to the same
string, and `_optionality.yml` and `optionality.yml` likewise. On this store that produced **3
false-positive groups out of 92**, all inside the legitimate `Condense comments in <path>` epic.
The discriminator is **file impact**: each of those six tickets carries one distinct path matching
its own title. Detector A should treat a collision whose members have DISTINCT file impact as
non-duplicate, or at minimum weight it down.

**2. Recurring alert filings always collide by title.** Eight tickets authored
`rebar-bridge[bot]` are recurring `[binding-drift] bridge-fsck found ...` alerts filed over
months. They are legitimate repeated filings, not duplicates, and a title-collision predicate will
flag them forever. Detector A needs an exemption path — by author, by tag, or by an explicit
recurring-filing marker.

Neither of these is hypothetical; both were measured on the live store while inventorying the 425.

## Dispatch status and the blocker

NOT dispatched as of 2026-09-05 ~20:40Z, for a FILE-OVERLAP reason rather than a priority one:

- `infra/terraform/monitoring_*.tf` — Gerrit change **2683** ("Stop treating a publish gap as an
  alarm breach") is in review touching nine `monitoring*.tf` files.
- `infra/scripts/observability.sh` — an agent is actively fixing the probe truncation
  (`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` / 9313), which is the same file this detector must publish from.

Implementing here now would collide on both. This ticket should be dispatched once 2683 merges and
the probe fix lands. Note also that the probe work is a PREREQUISITE in substance, not only in
scheduling: today's probe truncates and drops tail metrics at 31-53% presence, so a new metric
published late in `observability.sh` would inherit that truncation and the detector would be
unreliable in exactly the burst conditions it exists to catch.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OBSERVATION
This ticket already contains a complete RCA in its description and comments. I verified the key code paths: `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:create_ticket` returns only a per-call `duplicate_warning`; `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:duplicate_create_warning` computes same-normalized-title matches under `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` and returns an advisory string; `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_pass.py` prints the already-computed per-pass `outbound_differ create=` count. None of these paths persists an aggregate duplicate/title-collision count, a creation-volume metric, or an alarm signal.

HYPOTHESIS
Already-confirmed mechanism stands: rebar has two local signals that would detect mass creation (`duplicate_create_warning` title collisions, and reconciler/local CREATE volume), but both are emitted only at the producing call/pass. Because no independent observer aggregates them, a producer can create hundreds of tickets while every individual warning/counter remains effectively invisible.

CONFIRMATION
Verified by code inspection against the existing RCA: the duplicate warning path returns a string to the caller and swallows advisory failures; the reconciler path emits `RECON: outbound_differ total=... create=...` as text and does not feed a durable metric/alarm. The earlier comments already contain the historical replay numbers and the correction that title-collision alone would not catch the 2026-09-04 distinct-title surge. I did not re-run destructive historical replay; the existing RCA is complete and internally consistent with the current code.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Proceed with the ticket's two-detector design: an independent host/store observer that aggregates (1) same-normalized-title excess creations using the exact existing rule and (2) title-independent CREATE volume, publishes unclamped metrics, and alarms with cadence/missing-data choices justified against the recorded baselines.

comments.body: RCA/update: duplicate-title detection already existed only as per-call duplicate_warning from recent-creates; creation volume existed only implicitly as raw CREATE events / reconciler per-pass create counts. Neither produced an aggregate observer metric, so mass creation was silent unless a human saw each advisory/log line. The implemented fix adds independent read-only store metrics for rolling-hour duplicate-title excess and rolling-hour CREATE volume, using the same normalize_title rule as duplicate_warning, suppressing documented distinct-file-impact and recurring bridge-alert false positives, returning measured zeroes for empty windows, and leaving bridge/enrichment queues out of the signal path. RED: pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics.py -q failed on missing duplicate_title_peak_hour/create_volume_peak_hour before production changes. Verification: targeted tests passed; historical replay fired duplicate detector for 2026-08-31/09-01 and volume detector for 2026-09-04/05 while baseline 2026-08-20..25 stayed below threshold; make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=8 passed.

compiled_state.description:
## The gap

rebar ALREADY detects duplicate creation. `create_ticket` surfaces a `duplicate_warning` when the advisory in `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py` finds another ticket whose title matches under the shared pure `normalize_title` predicate (`recent_creates.py:55`; `duplicate_create_warning` begins at `:134`; `RECENT_WINDOW_NS` defines the 600s journal horizon). `_lib_writes.py`, `types.py`, and `_mcp_writes.py` are surfacing sites only.

But it is **advisory and per-call**. `_warn_advisory` hands the string back to the caller and that is
the end of it. Nothing counts these, publishes a metric, or alarms. So a writer creating hundreds of
duplicates emits hundreds of individual advisories that no human reads.

## TWO detectors are required, not one — corrected by the RCA

The 2026-09-05 RCA (`bafc-2f85-836f-4bdd`) established that a title-collision detector **would not
have caught the incident that prompted this ticket**. Both signals are needed:

**(a) Duplicate titles.** Confirmed as the right predicate for the duplicate population: all 425
excess tickets are found by exactly the normalized-title rule `duplicate_warning` already uses, and
that warning would have fired on every one.

**(b) Creation VOLUME.** The ~1,700-ticket surge that drove the Jira flood had **distinct titles**
(`Condense comments in <path>`, one per repo file), so (a) is blind to it. The signal that would have
caught it is rate: fixed UTC-hour CREATE buckets went 4-9 -> 62 -> 184 -> **968** -> 318; the implemented rolling-hour local-store replay peaks at **1010** because the 60-minute window can straddle fixed UTC bucket boundaries. The per-pass
`create=` counter in the reconciler's `outbound_differ` is likewise already computed and already
thrown away (baseline 0-4, surge peak 1180).

Both are rebar-side, so neither inherits the ACLI 1,200-issue ceiling.

## Why detect in rebar rather than Jira

A Jira-side detector is bounded by the ACLI per-query ceiling — the constraint whose workaround was
initially suspected of causing this incident. A detector that can be blinded by the class of defect it
watches for is not a detector. rebar's store has no such limit.

## The detector must be independent of the bridge

Do NOT emit these metrics from the reconciler. A malfunctioning bridge must not be responsible for
reporting its own malfunction — a dead-man inversion this repo has already paid for
(`herbal-garish-monkey`, `illbred-sour-alpaca`). The bridge runs in GitHub Actions
(`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`), so a host-side observer reading the store is independent
by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A duplicate-title metric counts same-normalized-title creations over a window, derived from the
      SAME pure `recent_creates.normalize_title()` predicate `duplicate_warning` uses.
- [x] A creation-VOLUME metric counts ticket CREATE events per hour, independent of title. Without
      this the alarm misses the incident that prompted it.
- [x] Both are published by an observer that does NOT depend on the bridge running, demonstrated with
      reconciliation stopped.
- [x] Alarms fire on rates consistent with mass creation, not ordinary operation. Justify against the
      RCA numbers: duplicate baseline 0-2/day vs 88/hr, so **count > 10 per rolling hour**; volume baseline 4-9/hr vs 968 fixed UTC-hour bucket / 1010 rolling-hour replay.
- [x] `treat_missing_data`, `evaluation_periods` and `datapoints_to_alarm` chosen against measured
      cadence, with reasoning recorded, and an explicit statement of why the combination cannot
      reproduce `illbred-sour-alpaca`'s false-page or unclearable-alarm behaviour.
- [x] No clamping anywhere in either metric path.
- [x] Defect-seeded: synthesise a burst in a test store, confirm each metric rises and its alarm
      condition is met; remove it and confirm it clears.
- [x] [non-codebase] Replay proof: duplicate window `2026-08-31T06:00:00Z..2026-09-01T04:00:00Z` asserts duplicate peak_hour=85/alarm true; volume window `2026-09-04T21:25:00Z..2026-09-05T03:00:00Z` asserts rolling-hour peak_hour=1010/alarm true; baseline `2026-08-20T00:00:00Z..2026-08-25T00:00:00Z` asserts duplicate=1 and volume=34 below threshold.
  provenance: environment=local worktree /Users/joeoakhart/bug-seahorse-duplicate-metrics at 84e94070c819934e053f8883b4719cd215b14d7d; principal=Copilot CLI agent; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — replay reads the local ticket-store history with the merged metric code and no bridge-side counters.
- [x] Portability: local store read plus host metric publish; no dependence on any single CI provider.

## Testing

1. RED first: with the detectors absent, show both windows produce no signal.
2. Unit: the normalized-title rule matches `duplicate_warning`'s, proven by driving both on the same
   inputs rather than by reading the code.
3. Replay both historical windows above.
4. With no reconciler/bridge process running, invoke `rebar metrics --since W0 --until W1 --output json` against a seeded store and assert both metrics are present and computed.

## Provenance

Operator-requested after the 2026-09-05 incident. RCA `bafc-2f85-836f-4bdd` corrected the original single-title-detector plan: the 09-05 surge had distinct titles, so volume detection is required too.

## Implementation clarification after scope review

The bridge-independent observer surface for this bug is the existing `rebar metrics --since/--until --output json` read command. The two new `src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py` derivations read durable CREATE/FILE_IMPACT event files directly from the local store via the existing generic event-file helper, so they do not depend on the Jira bridge, GitHub Actions, or any CI provider. The same computation can be called by the host observability publisher (`infra/scripts/observability.sh`) on its existing systemd timer and EC2 instance role if/when operators choose to wire CloudWatch publishing; this change deliberately does not edit Terraform per operator constraint.

Alarm semantics are represented in the metric value as `{peak_hour, alarm_threshold, alarm}` with no clamping. Duplicate-title uses `alarm_threshold=10`, matching the RCA baseline of 0-2/day versus 88/hour burst. Creation-volume uses `alarm_threshold=50`, above the observed baseline windows (4-9/hour steady; replay baseline peak 34/hour) and far below the incident peaks (968 fixed UTC-hour bucket; 1010 rolling-hour replay). Empty windows return measured zeroes instead of unavailable, so missing data cannot itself create a false page or unclearable alarm; absence of the metrics command/publisher output is an observer-liveness problem for the existing host heartbeat path rather than a breaching datapoint in either metric.


## Plan-review reconciliation (2026-09-08)

The duplicate-title metric shares only the pure `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py::normalize_title()` predicate with `duplicate_warning`; it does not call or depend on `duplicate_create_warning()`, the 600s `recent-creates.json` journal, or `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`. Therefore the create-time advisory and the aggregate metric cannot disagree on title equivalence, while legitimately using different windows and data sources.

Exact alarm comparisons are strict greater-than: duplicate-title alarms when rolling-hour excess duplicate creations are `> 10`; creation-volume alarms when rolling-hour CREATE events are `> 50`. Unit tests seed both below/above-threshold and clear paths, including empty windows as measured zeroes. Replay numbers are canonicalized in the [non-codebase] AC above: 1010 is the rolling-hour local-store oracle; 968 is the RCA fixed UTC-hour bucket; bridge-side outbound_differ counts (1180/985) are not used.

file_impact.reason: adds independent rolling-hour duplicate-title and create-volume store metrics
defect-seeded tests for duplicate/title volume alarms, false-positive suppressions, empty windows, and clear behavior
future host observer/publish integration point; current task constraints forbid terraform changes and this patch keeps the bridge-independent computation in rebar metrics

compiled_state.title: Duplicate ticket creation is detectable in rebar but nothing aggregates or alarms on it, so a reconciler creating hundreds of duplicates is silent
